We derived anisotropical Tolman - Oppenehmey-Volkov equations directly and then integrated them by reconstruction. We found that three generating conditions for one-fluid cases also work here to create multiple two fluids. These conditions yield the new exact solutions.

While most current Sequence-to-Sequence (Seq2Seq) Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) techniques primarily concentrate on generating extensive pseudo-training data to improve performance, very few tackle the challenge of few-shot domain adaptation. This study redefines various GEC environments as distinct tasks and introduces a methodology that applies few-shot meta-learning for domain adaptation entirely without synthetic pseudo data. By leveraging large data sets from source domains as anchors, we aim to create initial model parameters that enable rapid adaptation to new, low-resource target domains. Our approach specifically refines GEC capabilities across first languages (L1) acquired by learners developing non-native proficiency. Using nine diverse L1s as sources for meta-initialization and five additional L1s as target areas, we evaluate the system on paired datasets of clean and labeled noisy corpus. Experimental findings demonstrate significant improvements, with average F_1 scores increasing by 3.3 for individual domains and by 6.6 when assessed against strong baselines.

This paper examines the allocation of indivisible goods among strategic agents with additive valuation functions, operating in a non-monetary setting where a mechanism is algorithmic and relies solely on reported valuations. The primary objective is to identify mechanisms that guaranteed Pure Nash Equilibrium (PNE) outcomes while simultaneously ensuring a degree of fairness. We introduce the concept of "EF1 with budget balance (EBB-EF1)," which combines EBB-Efficiency with Envy-freeness up to one good (EF1) to guarantee fairness alongside balanced budget constraints. Our main contribution establishes an exact EBB-Efficiency mechanism; although this specific approach does not ensure EBB-EF1, it guarantees that every item goes to the highest bidder. We further analyze a family of related local clearing mechanisms and demonstrate the presence of PNE within them. Furthermore, we prove that budget balance limits the mechanism's performance ratio to approximately 1.84, a result supported by an asymptotically tight lower bound of 5/3. Finally, we address localized clearing strategies applicable to specific valuation classes, yielding constant max-min fairness ratios for such groups. Additionally, we establish and derive a bound of 4/3 (which includes the balanced budget constraint) for localized clearing fairness ratios for additive valuations, proving the tightness of this result.

The low surface brightness (LSB) spiral UGC 8839 rarely exhibits stellar formation, with a notable exception being a massive HII region complex situated at its outermost disc edge. To investigate the origins and characteristics of this cluster, researchers compared new Hα images alongside archival photometric images of UGC 8839 against similar data for four comparable spiral galaxies. The findings indicate that the off-center star formation in UGC 8839 arises from a hyper-stable, dark matter-dominate disc; in this system, the stability limit exists solely when reaching a minimum in the outermost disc regions. Furthermore, by adopting an analytical framework robust against the challenges of low surface brightness objects and sparse statistics, the study determines that such complexes are not anomalous if the HII region luminosity follows a power law, implying the structure is native rather than a merged satellite. However, a distinct bias toward larger radii for HII regions in UGC 8839 was observed relative to those found in the comparison galaxies. UGC 8839 effectively illustrates the correlation between the dark-to-barionic mass ratio and disc stability. Finally, a three-body interaction—a smaller-scale counterpart to forces hypothesized behind the phenomenon in Malin 1—is proposed as the consistent explanation for the extreme outer disc star formation.

Excellent signals were observed for all pertinent Wick contractions, except for a single instance. We analyzed the dependency of our findings on quark mass to evaluate whether correlations among quarks and antiquark constituents significantly influence the results. The regulation of protoplanetary disk evolution relies on analyzing how accretion rates scale with star and disk attributes; however, utilizing the distribution of these relations as a constraint on evolutionary models requires accurately accounting for accretion fluctuations. While this effect may be significant during embedded phases, it has often been considered minor in later stages. We present observations of XX Cha demonstrating nearly an order of magnitude (2 dex) variation in its accretion rate between 2010 and 2021. Comparisons between X-Shooter spectra taken during this interval and 19 years apart highlight this substantial change. Regardless of specific timing uncertainties, XX Cha exhibits extreme variability uncommon among classical T Tauri stars. Such widespread behavior could necessitate revisions to models currently constrained by observed accretion spreads. We note that previous spectral line analyses might have underestimated variability in certain objects, suggesting that timescales of fluctuation could extend longer than previously detected, thereby increasing their impact on population studies of classical T Tauri stars.

Offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) focuses on learning effective multi-agent strategies from collected historical data, playing a crucial role in preparing systems for real-world deployment. A prevalent practical challenge is that individual behavior policies generating joint agent trajectories often exhibit varying performance levels—for instance, mixing a completely random policy with more competent medium-valued policies. In the context of cooperative games with global reward structures, standard offline MARL approaches frequently allow agents trained on random data patterns to undermine overall team performance. This study explores offline MARL with a specific focus on addressing agent-level trajectory diversity by introducing the Shared Individual Trajectories (SIT) framework. Central to our approach, the credit assigned to specific agents is determined via a differentiable key-value memory interface using an attention-based reward decomposition network (RDN). Validated within a multi-agent environment featuring complex, non-stationary dynamics and extended across real-world applications, our experiments confirm that the proposed method effectively identifies and enhances high-quality trajectories while successfully transferring the learned experience to new settings. Through this, agents contributing random or disruptive actions receive diminished credit, ensuring only beneficial experiences are reinforced with corresponding performance upgrades.

We introduce a two- to three-dimensional medical image registration framework grounded in deep learning, designed to overcome the inherent low quality of megavoltage (MV) images by automatically generating high-quality representations for use with conventional methods. Most existing deep learning approximation strategies depend on large, manually curated datasets of paired intensity images to teach learned metrics, necessitating significant effort and time for annotation. To circum these issues, our approach first trains a generative model using an unsupervised method to convert an MV image into a high-resolution representation via another's inverse operation; this refined representation is then plugged into traditional optimization techniques. As an improvement to the other's learned distribution, we have integrated a discriminant model and refine the training of the generator with a nuanced loss to ensure that the training distribution matches the original input more closely. Since no pair markings are needed, this method offers a promising pathway to advance image matching capabilities across the clinical domain, particularly in tumor treatment planning involving IGRT, where it can mitigate the challenges and lack of utility associated with MV image analysis.

The integration of Artificial Intelligence and advanced information technology offers substantial benefits to the Internet of Vehicles (IoVs), yet it simultaneously introduces heightened security and privacy risks. Consequently, privacy preservation methods have become a major focus within research literature, although these solutions currently require specific adaptations to align with evolving IoVs architectures. Meanwhile, Federated Learning has emerged as a promising approach to mitigate privacy and security concerns within IoVs, complementing the robust, secure, distributed, and verifiable data sharing capabilities offered by Blockchain technology. This paper presents a comprehensive survey examining Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning frameworks specifically for IoVs. Additionally, the authors explore potential challenges, proposed solutions, and future research avenues associated with these BC-enabled FL frameworks. Ultimately, this survey provides a foundational framework for developing contemporary BC-enabled FL solutions designed to address various IoVs data privacy complexities and real-world scenarios.

This paper examines physical layer security (PLS) within a dual-hop wireless system utilizing OFDM architectures. The primary objective involves enhancing the system's secure end-to-end rate, composed of individual secrecy rates for each subcarrier. Given the independence between carrier components, each segment is analyzed separately before recombination via appropriate combination methods. Two specific scenarios are investigated in detail: the first assumes both communication nodes (source, relay, and legs) employ discrete phase shift (PS) precoding patterns, addressing estimation of the distribution for individual subcarrier legitimacy and utilization of these parameters for dual-hop optimization; the second scenario posits that while communication nodes have limited hardware constraints for precise feedback, the relay possesses highly constrained resolution capabilities, also requiring calculation of subindividual optimization. Key findings include observing that optimizing/subcarrier parameters cannot follow identical strategies across different equipment capacities. Two distinct optimization approaches are introduced to accommodate these variations: one for equipment with low capacity constraints and another for scenarios involving strict hardware limitations at the relay node. All results are supported by extensive simulations to validate theoretical formulations.

Text-based games provide an excellent framework for evaluating language comprehension, complex problem-solving, and common-sense inference in virtual agents, yet their performance scores often remain low because of inconsistencies between specific textual actions and the underlying game state. This model introduces no additional parameters to the agent's policy and claims to preserve existing performance levels while significantly simplifying the process of text-based game training.

Long short-term memory (LSTMs) have proven effective for addressing various natural language processing (NLP) applications. However, the widespread scale of parameters in these architectures is a critical concern that must be addressed to mitigate costs and maintain performance. In response to the scale requirement highlighted by recent works like Distilled Transformers and BERTBase, we observe that parameter counts for LSTM components such as the hidden update, forget, and output gates currently lack reduction, leading to redundancy that benefits could be exploited. In this paper, we introduce Narrow Gate LSTM (NGL), a novel architecture designed to deliver a more compact version of the LSTM. Our experiments demonstrate that NGLS outperforms standard Lsms, existing compressed architectures, and various BERT variations on both pretrained language tasks (including NGL's performance on NL-based language modeling (NL) and sentence level sentiment analysis tasks) and sentence level sentiment analysis tasks. In other words, using our new compression technique, we can achieve better results than with an uncompressed BERT-base model on both natural language understanding (NU) and machine translation tasks. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in transforming audio-visual data into meaningful sentences, we applied NGLS to a text-to-text generation task with encouraging performance in both pretrained and zero-shot settings, as shown by superior evaluation metrics across multiple datasets for better generalization in practical applications.

The Weak Gravity Conjecture is conventionally formulated as a limit on a particle's mass-to-charge ratio. While alternative versions suggest a formulation based on a particle's short-range repulsive force relative to long-range attraction—the so-called Dominant Ray Conjecture—this paper examines the compatibility of these versions within $\mathcal{N}=2$ conformal field theories (specifically linearized $\mathcal{N}=2$ CFT gravity). We identify a particle with zero radius of gravitational interaction and maximal repulsive force in this framework. Furthermore, we demonstrate a general scheme to generate a spectrum whose convexity in charge space closely mirrors that of the dominant ray, and we speculate on a universal principle extending this observation. Finally, we provide evidence supporting the conjecture that such convexity holds universally across all consistent CFTs, potentially serving as an independent criterion for Coniformal field theories.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are now integral to many safety-critical computer vision tasks, such as automated driving and human-robot collaboration. This article examines a data completion problem for time-harmonic Maxwell equations regarding the electric field within a bounded domain. The goal involves reconstructing incomplete information from an impenetrable boundary segment using measurements obtained from an accessible part. The research investigates a non-iterative quasi-reversibility approach and introduces several alternative mixed variational formulations. Proofs are provided to establish the well-posedness, convergence, and regularity of the problem. Furthermore, after finite element discretization utilizing edge elements, diverse three- and two-dimensional numerical simulations demonstrate the method's efficacy, even when applied to data containing noise.

In this work, we investigate Federated Selective Aggregation (FedSA), an approach designed to train a student model for a specific new task using contributions from multiple decentralized teacher models with distinct and self-contained prior training. This study addresses a current challenge in model sharing, where significant investments are made toward creating robust networks that cannot be distributed due to concerns regarding privacy, security, or intellectual rights. While existing federated methods may help, our proposal goes further by enabling the student to specialize entirely differently than its source teacher models. To address this, we develop an agent-driven strategy where a unique saliency mechanism adaptatively identifies which teachers should be selected to inject specific capabilities. Evaluations in both single and multi-task environments show that FedSA successfully merges insights from these fragmented resources to deliver performance on par with centralized approaches.

Assuming $\mathrm{rk}(E/\mathbb{Q}) \leq 1$ and that the curve lacks certain exceptional sub-2-descent obstructions, we demonstrate that there exist infinitely many such $S_4$ and $A_4$ extensions with a rank increment of precisely 0, 1, or 2. Furthermore, by employing the methods developed by S. Balakrshnan in the companion work [1], we establish the existence of a subset of these extensions—also comprising infinitely many $S_4$ and $A_4$ cases—where the elliptic curve's rank remains unchanged, a result when balanced against the potential for increase established previously. The quantum null energy condition (QNEC) establishes a lower limit on the energy-momentum tensor, relating it to how the entanglement entropy of a sub-region varies along a null direction. Investigating the quantum thermodynamics of many-body systems within two-dimensional holographic theories, the authors examine whether the QNEC constrains irreversible entropy production during dynamics. The study demonstrates that while pure states are subject to a strict version of the QNEC—requiring non-decreased total entropy after such processes—the condition for mixed states must include an additional upper bound on entrophy production. We examine the internal coherence of electroweak symmetry breaking, alongside phenomenological frameworks for neutrinos and dark matter, using the minimal scoto-seesaw model. By extending the simplest "missing partner" Type-I seesaw with the minimal dark sector, we establish a clear framework for neutrino oscillation bascilities: the atmospheric mass generation emerges from tree-level seesaw mechanisms, whereas the solar mass scale is radiatively corrected and facilitated via interaction with the dark sector. Specifically pinpointed parameter regions satisfy diverse experimental requirements regarding dark matter relic density, current detection limits (both theoretical constraints for direct searches), as well as vacuum stability derived through numerical solutions of two-loop renormalization group equations, which further confirms consistent dark parity invariance. Additionally, we demonstrate a putative limit for neutrinoless two-neutrino decay signal intensification.

We analyze the mixing between $e_g$ and $t_{2g}$ $d$-orbital states within a cubic lattice, likely present in many transition metal oxides (TMOs), using a Hubbard-like Hamiltonian. By solving this model analytically, we determine that substantial mixing can arise from a sizeable crystal field splitting between singly and doubly occupied states—corresponding to different spin configurations—and potentially from exchange interactions with surrounding electrons. Our approach is distinct from prior generic $sd$-mixing studies due to the explicit consideration of orbital and spin degrees of freedom within the same framework. This allows us to connect directly with the precise spin and orbital configurations relevant to branching ratio interpretations of TMOs $d$-absorption spectra. Consequently, absorption spectra with high mixing levels must be evaluated differently; where such conditions exist, simple standard models are insufficient, and branching ratios require re-examination. We illustrate these findings by re-examining the previously challenging case of NiO, demonstrating how accounting for $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ mixing resolves the long-standing discrepancy in its experimental versus theoretical absorption spectra branching ratios.

This study offers a preliminary feasibility test, demonstrating a move beyond the early-stage application of GANs to natural imagery found in medical contexts. Extends the Cyclic Reverse Generator approach by implementing an encoder engineered to faithfully disentangle the generator with synthetic X-rays while recolor with organ-level reconstruction, all within the care of a supervision token representing specific pathologies. The output of this labeled editing process provides source codes for retouching, allowing the model to generate specific retouchings that appear real and exhibit the intended medical conditions. The results of this paper show high realism in terms of image distribution and contain strong conditioning on visible labels for joint visualization. ViDaExpert serves as a specialized utility for the visualization and analysis of multidimensional vectorial datasets. Designed to handle "object-feature" formatted tables—controlling both numerical attributes and textual row/column labels—it integrates a suite of statistical techniques, including standard and weighted Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Elastic Maps (offering a non-linear approach to PCA), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and multilinear regression, alongside K-Means clustering and decision-tree construction variants. Featuring an array of intuitive dialogs for configuring data point properties such as size, shape, and color, along with rapid 3D rendering capabilities, ViDa Expert functions as a powerful instrument. This enables users to generate interactive 3D scenes representing high-dimensional data tables while efficiently executing both foundational and sophisticated statistical analyses.
